title: Request Decomposition Method
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Universal Engineering Research Coordinator Database (public edition), a database that decomposes requests, selects specialist databases, commissions generators, coordinates simulations, and assembles verified deliverables, as architecture coordinator for the NASA collection. Request Decomposition Method covers the following: breaks a request into tasks with inputs, outputs, and acceptance criteria for each. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Design targets only: labels in this record describe design targets for engineering work, never a claim of NASA, DARPA, or contractor qualification or approval. As architecture coordinator for the NASA collection, this pair decomposes requests, selects specialist databases, commissions generators, coordinates simulations, and assembles verified deliverables.

How it works

A coordination record decomposes a request into tasks, selects the specialist database for each task, commissions generators and simulations where needed, runs verification gates on every part, and assembles only gate-passing parts into the deliverable. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: breaks a request into tasks with inputs, outputs, and acceptance criteria for each. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo decomposes a request into tasks and prints tasks, gates passed, and parts assembled. The demo program prints:

Tasks decomposed: 5
Verification gates passed: 5/5
Deliverable parts assembled: 5
Open gaps delivered as gaps: 0

Use and limits

The coordinator assembles verified parts; it never invents a missing part. A task with no passing specialist result is delivered as an open gap, not filled with an unverified substitute. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record details

Record fields: request: plain-language request; specialist_selected: matched specialist database; generator_commission: commissioned generator task; verification_gate: gate check with verdict; task_class: retrieval of existing records.
demo_code:
tasks = 5
gates_passed = 5
print('Tasks decomposed: ' + str(tasks))
print('Verification gates passed: ' + str(gates_passed) + '/' + str(tasks))
print('Deliverable parts assembled: ' + str(gates_passed))
print('Open gaps delivered as gaps: ' + str(tasks - gates_passed))
demo_output:
Tasks decomposed: 5
Verification gates passed: 5/5
Deliverable parts assembled: 5
Open gaps delivered as gaps: 0

This record belongs to the Universal Engineering Research Coordinator Database (public edition), a database that decomposes requests, selects specialist databases, commissions generators, coordinates simulations, and assembles verified deliverables, as architecture coordinator for the NASA collection. Escalation Procedure covers the following: escalates a task that fails its gate twice, with its evidence packet attached. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Design targets only: labels in this record describe design targets for engineering work, never a claim of NASA, DARPA, or contractor qualification or approval. As architecture coordinator for the NASA collection, this pair decomposes requests, selects specialist databases, commissions generators, coordinates simulations, and assembles verified deliverables.

How it works

A coordination record decomposes a request into tasks, selects the specialist database for each task, commissions generators and simulations where needed, runs verification gates on every part, and assembles only gate-passing parts into the deliverable. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: escalates a task that fails its gate twice, with its evidence packet attached. The record sits at ladder rank compounded in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo decomposes a request into tasks and prints tasks, gates passed, and parts assembled. The demo program prints:

Tasks decomposed: 9
Verification gates passed: 9/9
Deliverable parts assembled: 9
Open gaps delivered as gaps: 0

Use and limits

The coordinator assembles verified parts; it never invents a missing part. A task with no passing specialist result is delivered as an open gap, not filled with an unverified substitute. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record details

Record fields: request: plain-language request; specialist_selected: matched specialist database; generator_commission: commissioned generator task; verification_gate: gate check with verdict; task_class: generation of complete, usable files and programs.

print('Deliverable parts assembled: ' + str(gates_passed))
print('Open gaps delivered as gaps: ' + str(tasks - gates_passed))
